column1: Perhaps not surprisingly, Bloom and Van Reenen report substantial heterogeneity in the quality of management. In each of the four countries, some firms are well run and some are badly run. More noteworthy is that the distribution of management quality differed substantially across the four nations. Firms in the United States have the highest average grade, followed by Germany, then France, and finally the United Kingdom. Much of the cross-country variation comes from the prevalence of especially badly run firms: firms with the lowest management grades are much more common in the United Kingdom and France than they are in the United States and Germany.
